doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: St. Louis 1904 job and funeral marches
summary: Laine tells of his men at a St. Louis garden in 1904, the size of funeral bands, Under Arms as the main march, and that he learned notes from Perkins.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I had a trunk load of that stuff.
I got this picture. She put it all up.
Well, do you remember whether it was back in the 90s or in... Oh, yeah.
Way back when you first started having a brass band.

Because in 1904, some of my boys played an artificial garden in St. Louis for the Grand View Portainal Hotel. It was an artificial garden. Yeah. An artificial garden, see. And I went up there, I believe, for two weeks, I think it was. They asked me to come up there. Now, there was only three of the boys went up there, my boys, but they had five in that band. They used two from up there. The piano player they used and the drum player from up there they used. See. Now, the carnet and the clarinet player and the bass player was from here, my men. They asked me to come up there one time, you know. I kind of managed to squeeze in to find a little time to go up there. And brother, you take it from me. When I left, you almost cried. And, uh... You know, at the time, not to speak about myself being wonderful on that, but I really was.
You had a good band on that band.

Oh, remarkable. And I couldn't feel the engagements. I'm going to tell you just right now, I couldn't feel the engagements. But did they have funerals about the time of the St. Louis trip? They were about winding up around that time in 1904. Yes, I believe it was about winding up around that time, funerals, yeah.
How big a band did you use for that, for the funerals? Ten or twelve.

Ten or twelve. And what kind of music did you play? All marches, dead marches, all funeral marches. All funeral marches. Our main piece was a piece they called Under Arms. And it was a march, it was a military march, at the same time you could use it for a burial march.
You had the music for that?
Oh, yes. You had the music. Oh, yes. I had the music for that, yeah.
Now, you see, most of the band didn't read. Most of my boys didn't read. Only a couple of them did. See?

A couple of them did. Now, what I've learned was through Perkins. You know how I learned in the notes, it was through Perkins. See? Yeah. He'd teach me and show me just what to do and where to make my stops, where I make rows, where I have to beat before rows and so on. See? Well, then I got onto all of that very quick.
